- Budget range: ~$25k-$40k / month for Dedicated capacity initially

Initial sizing notes (very high-level):

- Production scale target: 8-12 GPUs reserved depending on final model and sequence length

Next steps I propose:
1) SE deep-dive with Marcus to validate perf and pick exact GPU type/size (Marcus, can we schedule a 60-minute deep-dive next week?)
2) I'll share a draft pricing worksheet and sample unit-economics scenarios (attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf and acme_estimated_usage.xlsx)
3) Procurement: confirm desired commitment term (12 vs 24 months) so I can surface committed-discount tiers

I'll loop in Marcus on the SE items - he can provide per-GPU throughput numbers and a deployment diagram. If this looks right, can you confirm the expected average sequence length (tokens per request) and whether you expect steady streaming traffic or large batch jobs? That'll change the recommended configuration.

Thanks - happy to adjust. Proposed SE slots: Wed/Thu next week (I'll coordinate availabilities).

Hi Maria / Marissa - quick SE notes from my side ahead of the deep-dive: 

Benchmark & sizing guidance (our internal numbers for the target model family you mentioned):
- H100 (perf-optimized): ~60k tokens/min per GPU for typical request shapes (batching enabled, sequence length ~512 tokens). Burst concurrency and batching can raise this but increases latencies.
- A100 (cost-optimized): ~35k tokens/min per GPU with similar batching + sequence length assumptions.

Implication for Acme targets:
- Sustained ~200k tokens/min: requires ~4 x H100 (60k * 4 = 240k) or ~6 x A100 (35k * 6 = 210k) to meet sustained throughput with headroom.
- Peak/burst ~1M tokens/min: design for autoscaling/burst pool. For short bursts we recommend a pre-warmed burst pool of 4 H100 or ~8 A100s (depending on GPU choice) with fast routing/fallback to shared capacity.

Latency & batching notes:
- If 95p latency requirement is <250ms, we'll need smaller batches and more GPUs (batches trade cost for latency). Please confirm your 95p SLO.
- Typical sequence length heavily impacts per-GPU throughput (512 tokens assumed above). If sequence length is shorter (e.g., 128 tokens) tokens/min per GPU can increase ~2-4x.

Items I'm attaching for the deep-dive: deployment_diagram.png, recent_benchmark_log.txt (summary in the attached PDF).

Requests for Acme ahead of the SE call:
1) Typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95 tokens per request)
2) Expected RPS distribution (steady vs spiky) and any large-batch offline jobs
3) Any strict latency SLOs at the 95p or 99p level

I'll prepare two concrete pricing + sizing options (A100 vs H100) with example $/1M tokens and monthly totals for 12-month commitment.

Thanks - Marcus
Marcus Lin
